sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion at this exact site
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface expression of the FLAG-tagged receptor was detected (construct generated specifically for surface detection); no explicit signalling or binding assay result reported in the clip.
sites.rationale: L1 names residues 94–101 (DKEAPTGS) as the replaced block; Python confirmed seq[93:101]='DKEAPTGS' exactly. The junction is insert_after_residue=93 (seq[92]='E'), with residue_after=seq[93]='D' (first residue of the replaced block). Position 93–101 lies deep within the large N-terminal ECD (landmarks: extracellular 27–186), 86 residues from TM1, well clear of any TM boundary. The nearest ECD cysteines are at positions 108 and 117, both outside the replaced block. Full-length human PTH1R construct in which residues 94–101 (DKEAPTGS, exon E2 region) were replaced by the FLAG sequence (DYKDDDDK) by PCR overlap extension; the tagged receptor was used to detect surface-expressed PTH1R in the absence of a commercial antibody.

sources.claim: Parathyroid hormone (PTH) regulates bone remodeling and calcium and phosphate homeostasis. PTH actions are mediated by type I PTH/PTH-related peptide receptor (PTH1R). There has been no commercially available, specific antibody to detect human PTH1R expression so far. Flag-tagged human PTH1R construct, converting the sequence DKEAPTGS (residues 94-101) in the exon E2 region of PTH1R to DYKDDDDK of Flag epitope, was generated by using PCR overlap extension or ligase enzyme for two-fragment assembly.

sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 770 ± 69.3 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface luminescence confirmed receptor at plasma membrane; agonist-induced internalization monitored via reduction in luminescence; activation behaviour described as similar to unmodified PTH1R (nLuc-PTH1R precedent cited).
sites.rationale: L4/L5/L6 explicitly state HiBiT is fused to the N-terminus of full-length PTH1R; the signal peptide spans residues 1–26 (landmarks), so the mature N-terminus is residue 27 and the tag sits at the 26/27 junction. Python confirmed seq[25]='V' and seq[26]='D'. This is the only extracellular terminus of PTH1R (C-terminus is intracellular, residues 463–593), making the junction unambiguous. L2 and L3 provide independent corroboration of the same junction with FLAG and HA tags respectively. Full-length PTH1R with HiBiT fused to its N-terminus (HiBiT-PTH1R) expressed in HEK293 cells; the tag is placed after the signal peptide cleavage site (mature N-terminus = residue 27), confirmed at the plasma membrane by LgBiT/substrate luminescence under non-permeabilized conditions. L2 (PMC12643933) independently places a FLAG tag at the identical junction ('between the HA signal sequence and PTH1R coding sequence'), and L3 (PMC8682804) reports stable MDCK cell lines expressing HA-tagged PTH1R at the cell surface.

sources.claim: We fused HiBiT to the N-terminus of the PTH1R (HiBiT-PTH1R).

literature_notes: L2 (PMC12643933) and L3 (PMC8682804) both support the N-terminal junction (insert_after_residue=26) with FLAG and HA tags respectively, but are subsumed into Site 1 because they pin the identical junction already validated with functional data by L4/L5/L6. L3 names no residue and would be topology_derived alone; L2 is validated but provides no functional assay result beyond 'used for structural and functional studies'. The best-evidenced clip (L4/L5/L6) is therefore used as the primary supporting_clip_id for Site 1. No ledger line supports any tag in ECL1 (242–282), ECL2 (343–357), or ECL3 (427–437). The C-terminus (residues 463–593) is intracellular and no snorkel construct is reported in the ledger.
